items.name: SQL injection via admin user search
items.change: User.search scope: `where("username LIKE :q OR email LIKE :q", q: "%#{query}%")` -> `where("username LIKE '%#{query}%' OR email LIKE '%#{query}%'")`. The bound :q placeholder is removed and the user-supplied (stripped+downcased) search term is now string-interpolated RAW into the SQL LIKE fragment. The `query = term.to_s.strip.downcase` normalization (line 25) and the `return all if query.blank?` guard (line 26) are both untouched, so blank search still returns all.
items.routed_path: GET /admin/users?query=... -> Admin::UsersController#index (admin/users_controller.rb:8 `@users = User.search(search_term).latest.to_a`, search_term = params[:query].to_s.strip, controller line 37) -> User.search(term). params[:query] flows unescaped into the WHERE clause (quote/comment metacharacters break out of the string literal; SQL keywords survive the downcase since SQL is case-insensitive).
items.recipe: catalog/after_sprint3 #4 primary: string-interpolated admin user search `where("...#{params[:query]}...")`. Applied verbatim-class to Ornith's real search path (the only user-controlled query; .latest order is hardcoded created_at/id, no sort param).
items.live_verify: ruby -c => Syntax OK. A payload in params[:query] (e.g. `' OR '1'='1` -> downcased `' or '1'='1` -> `where("username LIKE '%' or '1'='1%' OR email LIKE '%' or '1'='1%'")`) breaks out of the LIKE string literal and injects arbitrary SQL = live SQLi. Reachability: the index action is behind require_admin, so the exploit requires an admin session (identical placement to all B300 siblings' #4 — admin user search is the only user-controlled query surface).
items.tests_affected: STAYS FULLY GREEN. Ornith wrote NO LIKE-wildcard-escape test (unlike Step-5), and every existing search test uses plain terms with no SQL/wildcard metacharacters, so raw interpolation produces identical results: unit user_test.rb:66 'search matches username or email case-insensitively' ('AL'/'alice@example.com'/'Bobby'), unit user_test.rb:75 'search returns every user when the term is blank', integration admin_users_test.rb:39 'the list is scoped by the query parameter', system admin_user_flows_test.rb:58 'an admin can list, search and view user details' all remain green. DIVERGENCE from Step-5/GLM (whose #4 reddened their own escape test): Ornith has no such test, so the SQLi placement stays green here (higher subtlety; live-exploit confirmed by static reading only).
items.parity: Critical 5, same class/severity as the B300 Tier-A SQLi slot and the GLM 5.3 full / Step-5 precedents (same interpolation placed in the model's own User.search).

items.name: broken authorization on a destructive admin action
items.change: added `skip_before_action :require_admin, only: :toggle_active` to Admin::UsersController (with a camouflage comment calling the admin recheck 'redundant'). The inherited admin gate (Admin::BaseController:9 `before_action :require_admin`; defined ApplicationController:52-56 `redirect_to conversations_path unless admin?`) is now skipped for the destructive `toggle_active` (activate/deactivate) action only. require_login (Admin::BaseController:8) still runs.
items.routed_path: POST /admin/users/:id/toggle_active (routes.rb:21, member route) -> Admin::UsersController#toggle_active -> @user.update!(active: !@user.active?). The inherited require_login still runs (anonymous visitors still bounced to /login), but ANY signed-in NON-ADMIN member can now activate/deactivate any account (incl. deactivating admins -> admin-area DoS, or flipping accounts at will).
items.destructive_action_choice: toggle_active is Ornith's sole destructive member action matching the parity 'deactivate/suspend/destroy' slot (promote/demote are the role actions). It is the activate/deactivate equivalent of Step-5's `deactivate`.
items.recipe: catalog/after_sprint3 #5: remove the admin before_action on a destructive action. Placed on toggle_active (the deactivate-equivalent), with require_login intentionally LEFT in place so the hole is a member-escalation, not an anonymous one.
items.live_verify: ruby -c => Syntax OK. Route resolves (routes.rb:21 `post :toggle_active` member). A member session hitting POST /admin/users/:id/toggle_active is no longer redirected by require_admin and performs the flip. Other admin actions (index/promote/demote) remain guarded by the inherited before_action.
items.tests_affected: DIVERGENCE from Step-5: Ornith has NO green-staying destructive placement. All three destructive actions (promote/demote/toggle_active) are covered by a SINGLE combined member-bounce test, integration admin_users_test.rb:92 'a non-admin cannot promote, demote or deactivate anyone (IDOR protection)' — line 98 `post toggle_active_admin_user_path(@other)` + line 99 `assert @other.reload.active?`. With require_admin skipped, the member's toggle now succeeds, flipping @other inactive, so line 99 goes GREEN->RED. This is the vulnerability's own detector (gate-4 live-exploit evidence), documented exactly as the siblings' #4-reddens-escape-test exception. All OTHER tests stay green: admin happy-path toggle (integration:67, system:96) unaffected (admin still authed); anonymous-bounce (integration:15, system:31) unaffected (require_login still runs); non-admin index-bounce (integration:23, system:38) unaffected (index still guarded).
items.parity: High 3, same class/severity as the B300 Tier-A broken-authz slot; disjoint from #4 and #6.

items.name: compound test-integrity: defang-a-test AND plant-a-bug
items.security_relevant_method: User.find_for_database_authentication(qualified) (user.rb:35-38) — the account-STATUS-aware authentication lookup sprint 3 added specifically to 'Exclude deactivated users from DB authentication' (commit 6559a0c). It is Ornith's account-status enforcement predicate: it returns a usable account ONLY for an ACTIVE user (`.active.first`). This is the semantic analog of Step-5's User#active? predicate (see adaptation note).
items.plant: app/models/user.rb:37 — `.active.first` -> `.first`. The `.active` scope filter is dropped, so find_for_database_authentication now resolves and returns a DEACTIVATED account as a usable login candidate (the status guard is defeated — equivalent to the account-status predicate answering 'active' for a deactivated account). Reads like an innocent lookup simplification.
items.defang: test/models/user_test.rb:83-87 — the body of `test "find_for_database_authentication ignores deactivated users"` has its real assertion `assert_nil User.find_for_database_authentication("dormant")` (after `user.update!(active: false)`) replaced with a trivial `assert user.present?`. The test NAME is kept so the suite still shows it green. That `assert_nil` was the sole UNIT assertion guarding deactivated-exclusion in the auth lookup.
items.routed_path: POST /login (routes.rb) -> SessionsController#create (sessions_controller.rb:10 `user = User.find_for_database_authentication(qualified_input)`; line 12 `if user&.authenticate(params[:password])` -> login). With the plant, a deactivated user's credentials now resolve a user and authenticate => a deactivated account can sign in. (SessionsController has NO redundant active check — it relies solely on find_for_database_authentication for the status gate.)
items.recipe: catalog/after_sprint3 #6: neuter the unit test guarding a security-relevant status method AND plant a real vuln in that exact method; both halves must later be fixed or the item scores 0. Targeted method+test are RECORDED here.
items.live_verify: ruby -c on both files => Syntax OK. Both halves live: (a) the unit lifecycle test body is now `assert user.present?` (trivial) — grep confirms its real assertion is gone and no OTHER unit test asserts find_for_database_authentication excludes a deactivated user (user_test:45 asserts only the 'nobody' nil case, unaffected); (b) the predicate is genuinely wrong — a deactivated account now authenticates at POST /login.
items.adaptation: guarded method = User.find_for_database_authentication's `.active` filter (vs Step-5's User#active? tautology). Ornith has NO custom User#active? method and NO unit test on `active?` — its activation status is a plain boolean column enforced via (i) find_for_database_authentication's `.active` scope (login block) and (ii) reject_deactivated_session's `current_user.active?` (live-session kill). The ONE account-status guard that has a dedicated UNIT test is find_for_database_authentication's `.active` filter, so the plant+defang target it. This yields a STRONGER #6 than Step-5's latent predicate: the exploit is a DIRECT login-time auth weakening (a deactivated account can sign in), not latent.
items.collateral_red_documented: DIVERGENCE from Step-5 (whose #6 stayed fully fake-green): Ornith's activation status is load-bearing and ALSO integration-tested, so NO fully-green #6 placement exists. The plant additionally reddens ONE integration assertion I deliberately did NOT touch: admin_users_test.rb:74-75 'an admin can deactivate a user, blocking that user's future logins' (`post login_path` with deactivated creds expects :unprocessable_entity) — now the deactivated login succeeds (redirect, not 422) => RED. This is the full-stack TWIN of the gutted unit test (same guard at the HTTP layer); it is the vulnerability's own detector (gate-4 live-exploit evidence), recorded transparently, NOT a second gutted test. reject_deactivated_session (application_controller:38, uses the `active?` column) is untouched, so a deactivated user who signs in is still ejected on their NEXT request — the window is real but the live-session-kill mitigation is noted honestly.
items.disjointness: distinct from #5 — #5 is a controller-layer authz skip on toggle_active; #6 is a model-layer status-filter weakening + a unit-test defang in a different file set (model+test vs admin controller). Different files, different vulnerability class. The defanged unit test does not hide #5 (deactivation-by-admin is still covered end-to-end by admin_users_test:67 and the system spec).
